answer:
**RESPUESTA: 1 de 18 (5,56%) — IC 95% Wilson [0,99%, 25,76%]** de los estudios originales del proyecto de Experimentos Económicos (`project == "ee"`) se realizaron en Reino Unido.

**Hipótesis final (texto para la entrega, en inglés porque la pregunta lo es):**
"Among the original studies of the Experimental Economics replication project (project == 'ee') in this dataset, 1 of 18 (5.56%, 95% Wilson CI 0.99%-25.76%) were conducted in the United Kingdom: the single case is Huck, Seltzer and Wallace (AER 2011), id ee.13, n = 120, which was not replicated. The same proportion holds whether or not rows with a missing original country are excluded (1/18 = 5.56%), because no ee row has a missing country. The field is dominated by the United States (11/18 = 61.11%), followed by Germany and Switzerland (2 each) and by Australia and Austria (1 each), so being conducted in the UK was rare in this sample -- and it is not implied by language, since 13/18 originals used English yet only one was in the UK. Scope limit: these files contain only the 18 originals of the Experimental Economics project available here (16 in the American Economic Review, 2 in the Quarterly Journal of Economics), one row per original study with a single replication each. Any additional originals that a broader published catalogue of this replication project may contain are simply absent from these files, so this proportion is a property of these 18 sampled originals and is not an estimate of the full catalogue, about which these data support no claim."

**Workflow ejecutado (según tus decisiones)**
1. Población: `project == "ee"` en el CSV de estudio → 18 filas, **una por original** (ids ee.1–ee.18, títulos y autores únicos, 0 duplicados, 0 `drop`, 0 `aggregated`, 0 `lab_id`). Sin exclusiones.
2. Numerador: criterio **estricto** `experiment_country.o == "United Kingdom"` tras normalizar (minúsculas, espacios colapsados, punto final). Solo "United Kingdom" mapea a UK; Australia y los demás anglófonos quedan fuera.
3. Ambos denominadores: sin filtrar N=18 y país no nulo N=18 → **coinciden porque ee tiene 0 NaN de país** (declarado explícitamente en el log).
4. **El segundo CSV NO interviene en el cálculo**: 15 columnas y **cero columnas de país** (verificado: `[c for c in r.columns if 'countr' in c.lower()] == []`); su único rol fue la validación 1:1 de los 18 originales EERP por apellido del primer autor → ahora **EXACT 18/18** tras corregir la limpieza.
5. IC Wilson implementado a mano, **verificado por segunda vez de forma independiente** y contra `statsmodels` (Wilson [0.99, 25.76]; Clopper-Pearson [0.14, 27.29] como referencia de que el ancho es del tamaño muestral, no precisión).

**Integridad:** el 5,56% visto en la inspección queda **confirmado por el cálculo formal** (script definitivo con verificaciones de integridad y auditoría de las 18 filas), no repetido de la tabla exploratoria. Los artefactos de emparejamiento ("de Clippel"/"De Clippel" y el falso "funberg" generado por un `.replace('de',''))` quedan documentados en el log como artefactos de normalización de strings, no discrepancias reales.

payload.workflow: 1) Loaded meta-regression_study_data (927x57); filtered project=='ee' -> 18 rows, one per original study (unique ids ee.1-ee.18, titles, authors; 0 duplicates, 0 drop==True, 0 aggregated, 0 multi-lab). 2) Normalised experiment_country.o (lowercase, whitespace collapse, trailing dot) and applied the STRICT UK criterion against {united kingdom, uk, u.k, great britain, britain, england, scotland, wales}; only 'United Kingdom' matched. 3) Computed numerator (1) over both denominators: all ee rows (18) and rows with non-missing country (18) -- identical because ee has zero missing countries. 4) Computed the 95% Wilson interval by hand and verified it independently plus with statsmodels (Wilson 0.99-25.76; Clopper-Pearson 0.14-27.29 as a wider reference). 5) Built context tables (country, original language, journal x year) and the audit trail of all 18 originals. 6) The second CSV was NOT used in the computation because it has no country column (verified programmatically); its only role was the 1:1 validation of the 18 EERP originals by first-author surname (now EXACT 18/18 after fixing string-cleaning artefacts).
